title: Fastlane: build, screenshots, metadata and upload

videos.script:
By now a release is a dozen steps. {{steps}} Check the listing, check the privacy answers, check the certificates, build, sign, upload, and send the notes. Typed by hand, one of them is forgotten.

Fastlane is the tool most mobile teams use to put those steps in one file. {{fastlane}} It is written in Ruby, it runs on Linux and on a Mac, and it speaks to both stores.

Today you install it on your own computer and write the planner's first lanes. {{lanes}} One that runs every check from the earlier lessons and stops the release when one fails.

The lanes that upload need store accounts, so they are read here. {{read}} But they read the same listing folders you wrote in lesson 4, and that is the point: the files you already have are what Fastlane sends.
